note: Dated events that explain the regimes in the sample, each with the document it was read in, in this study's words. An event no readable document supports is not a row; left_out lists them with the reason.

events.what: The first export cargo of the shale era leaves Sabine Pass, the Asia Vision, for Brazil.
events.source: US Department of Energy, LNG monthly reports, transaction file

events.what: The first LNG carrier passes the expanded Panama Canal, the Maran Gas Apollonia from Sabine Pass.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, press release of 25 July 2016

events.what: Panama's neopanamax draught cut to 44 feet in the drought of 2019, from 49 in February; a further step to 43 feet was announced, postponed and suspended.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisories A-10-2019 of 1 April 2019, A-13, A-24 and A-26-2019

events.what: US cargoes cancelled: about 46 in June, 50 in July, 45 for August and 30 for September 2020, by EIA's estimate and the trade press it cites.
events.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 11 August 2020

events.what: JKM assessed at 32.494 $/MMBtu, the highest since Platts began assessing it in 2009, in the cold snap of January 2021; a cargo trades at 39.30.
events.source: Bloomberg, in gCaptain, 12 January 2021

events.what: Dutch front month gas rises more than 16 percent in a day to a record 171.40 EUR/MWh as flows on the Yamal pipeline reverse eastward.
events.source: Reuters, in gCaptain, 21 December 2021

events.what: Fire at Freeport LNG shuts the plant, 2 billion cubic feet a day and 17 percent of US export capacity; Henry Hub falls 1.27 $/MMBtu the next day.
events.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 23 June 2022

events.what: Nord Stream 1 stops for ten days of maintenance, 11 to 21 July 2022, with no assurance of its return.
events.source: Reuters, in gCaptain, 11 July 2022

events.what: Gazprom halts Nord Stream 1 for three days from 31 August; the week's TTF average of 83.62 $/MMBtu is the highest of the weekly series.
events.source: Reuters, in gCaptain, 21 August 2022; this study's weekly series

events.what: Freeport LNG cleared to restart its remaining trains, eight months after the fire; its first cargo since loads in February 2023.
events.source: LNG Prime, 9 March 2023

events.what: Panama cuts daily transits to an average of 32, 10 of them neopanamax, in the drought; queues of up to 21 days in August.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisory A-35-2023 of 25 July 2023; IEA, Global Gas Security Review 2024

events.what: Workers at Chevron's Gorgon and Wheatstone plants, over 5 percent of world supply, start industrial action; suspended on 22 September.
events.source: LNG Prime, 8 and 22 September 2023

events.what: Panama cuts booking slots to 25 a day, to fall to 22 in December and 18 in February 2024.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisory A-48-2023 of 30 October 2023

events.what: US cargoes bound for Asia turn from Suez to the Cape: a Cove Point cargo loaded on 16 December diverts round Africa for Japan, a Freeport cargo for Korea does the same.
events.source: Bloomberg, in gCaptain, 24 December 2023

events.what: The last laden LNG carrier passes Suez; Qatari carriers turn south and no LNG carrier crosses the Red Sea from mid January.
events.source: Oxford Institute for Energy Studies, NG-188, February 2024

events.what: Panama holds 24 booking slots a day, 7 of them neopanamax, with container ships ahead of LNG; LNG transits all but stop.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisory A-54-2023 of 15 December 2023, and A-08-2024; IEA

events.what: A record 27 US cargoes to Asia sail round the Cape of Good Hope in the month.
events.source: Platts, republished by Hellenic Shipping News, 22 April 2024

events.what: Panama back to normal operating conditions, 36 booking slots a day, 10 of them neopanamax.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisory A-28-2024 of 15 August 2024

events.what: Plaquemines LNG loads its first cargo, the eighth US export terminal; Corpus Christi Stage 3 follows in February 2025.
events.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 13 January 2025

events.what: The first LNG carrier in five months passes Bab el Mandeb.
events.source: gCaptain, 8 February 2025

events.what: China's tariff of 15 percent on US LNG and coal takes effect, in reply to the US tariffs of 4 February; China's imports of US LNG fall to zero by March.
events.source: Reuters, in gCaptain, 4 February 2025; Bloomberg, in gCaptain, 21 April 2025

events.what: China's tariff on all US goods raised to 84 percent, then 125 on 11 April, on top of the 15 on LNG.
events.source: Bloomberg and Reuters, in gCaptain, 9 and 11 April 2025

events.what: The Geneva step: China's 125 percent falls to 10 for ninety days; the 15 percent on US LNG stays, and the trade stays halted.
events.source: Bloomberg, in gCaptain, 12 May 2025

events.what: The Houthis announce a suspension of their maritime operations; container lines test the Red Sea again from February 2026.
events.source: gCaptain, 11 November 2025

events.what: US and Israeli strikes on Iran; Iran declares the Strait of Hormuz closed to all ships and Qatari gas tankers pause.
events.source: Reuters and Bloomberg, in gCaptain, 28 February 2026

events.what: QatarEnergy declares force majeure on its LNG exports, two days after halting production at Ras Laffan; gas prices and freight at multi year highs.
events.source: Reuters, in gCaptain, 4 March 2026

events.what: An Iranian missile strike damages Ras Laffan: two of Qatar's fourteen trains, 17 percent of its capacity, out for three to five years.
events.source: Bloomberg and Reuters, in gCaptain, 18 and 19 March 2026

events.what: Golden Pass LNG loads its first cargo, the ninth US export terminal.
events.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, Today in Energy, 23 April 2026

events.what: The first Qatari LNG cargo since the war crosses Hormuz by the northern route Iran allows, sold to Pakistan.
events.source: Bloomberg and Reuters, in gCaptain, 10 and 11 May 2026

events.what: US LNG is shipped to China again: EIA's table, which records the destination declared at departure, shows 4,576 MMcf by vessel in June and 4,555 in July, the first since 546 in September 2025; whether the LNG was used in China or shipped on is not established.
events.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, exports by country, release of 30 September 2026

events.what: An interim agreement between the US and Iran ends four months of hostilities and provides for a return to the maritime traffic of before the war.
events.source: Reuters, in gCaptain, 16 June and 5 July 2026

events.what: Panama's neopanamax draught cut in steps, 49.5 feet from 3 July 2026 to 48 feet from 2 September, and neopanamax slots to 9 a day from 4 September.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisories A-18, A-22, A-25, A-29 and A-33-2026

events.what: The US and China are reported to be discussing a cut to China's tariff on US LNG.
events.source: gCaptain, 19 September 2026, reporting Reuters of 18 September

events.what: Panama's neopanamax draught back to 49 feet at once, and 10 neopanamax slots a day for bookings from 15 October, 4 of them a week for LNG.
events.source: Panama Canal Authority, advisory A-36-2026 of 28 September 2026

left_out.what: JKM's record low of 28 April 2020, Cape voyages above one a day in November 2020 and 58 LNG transits of Panama in January 2021
left_out.reason: S&P Global's figures; this study does not request S&P Global's pages and found no republication of these

left_out.what: Russia's invasion of Ukraine on 24 February 2022
left_out.reason: no document on it was read for this study; the year shows in the spread, TTF above JKM for long stretches

left_out.what: The first attacks on shipping in the Red Sea, November 2023
left_out.reason: no dated document on them was read; the diversions are marked from 24 December 2023 and the closure of the route from 13 January 2024

left_out.what: The Suez Canal Authority's rebates for US Gulf LNG carriers and Panama's slot auctions
left_out.reason: rules of the canals, not events: they are in the tolls and on the Routes view's timeline

left_out.what: No US cargo reaching China from 6 February 2025
left_out.reason: a statement of April 2025 about arrivals, which EIA's table contradicts for September 2025

left_out.what: Spark's Atlantic rate jumping 163 percent on 3 March 2026
left_out.reason: Lloyd's List's figure, which this study does not request; LNG Prime's 161,750 $/day for 3 March is drawn as a charter rate

left_out.what: The JKM to TTF spread flipping from a European to an Asian premium in March 2026
left_out.reason: IEA's averages were not read; the spread itself is drawn

left_out.what: JKM and TTF reported on 18 September 2026 with the US arbitrage to Asia uneconomic
left_out.reason: Global LNG Hub's note was not read

left_out.what: Spark's first negative Atlantic rate, 8 February 2022, and its record of 374,000 $/day in October 2022
left_out.reason: charter rates, drawn as such on the breakeven hire panel

left_out.what: The EU ETS covering shipping and Spark's change of ship, January 2024
left_out.reason: breaks in the data, drawn as numbered rules
